declarations.name: CKSD.factorCovariance_mul_orthogonal
declarations.doc: Orthogonal rotations of factors do not change their implied covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.normalizedFactorLoading_eq_up_to_signs
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.35: normalized nondegenerate loadings are identified up to column signs once both their common covariance and the diagonal unique covariance are specified.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_factor_mle_of_compact
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.35: consistency of factor maximum likelihood on a compact identified parameter set. Compactness and uniform positive unique variances are explicit restrictions of this formulation; the unrestricted parameter-space and asymptotic-normality assertions are not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent
declarations.doc: The observed-history event `{L̄_k = l̄_k, Ā_{k-1} = ā_{k-1}}` for a covariate record `l`: the covariates up to time `k` take the recorded values and the treatments before time `k` follow the regime `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: The regime-adherent past `{L̄_{k-1} = l̄_{k-1}, Ā_{k-1} = ā_{k-1}}` before time `k`; it is the whole space for `k = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_congr
declarations.doc: History events depend only on the recorded covariates up to the current time.

declarations.name: CKSD.gRegimeEvent_congr
declarations.doc: Regime-adherent pasts depend only on the recorded covariates before the current time.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_subset_gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: The history event at time `k` is contained in the regime-adherent past before `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_snoc
declarations.doc: Appending the next covariate value splits the regime-adherent past.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_gHistoryEvent
declarations.doc: History events are measurable when the coordinate events are.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: Regime-adherent pasts are measurable when the coordinate events are.

declarations.name: CKSD.prod_div_succ_mul_eq_prod_div
declarations.doc: Telescoping of sequential weights: for real weights with the zero pattern of probabilities of nested events, the inverse treatment weights times the final probability equal the product of the conditional covariate probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_sum_gInverseWeight
declarations.doc: Inverse-probability-weighted representation over the first `n` time points. If at each time `k < N` the potential outcome is mean-exchangeable with the treatment given the observed history, and regime-adherent continuations of histories of positive probability have positive probability, then for `n ≤ N` the mean of `Ya` is the sum over covariate records of the inverse treatment weights times the integral of `Ya` over the regime-adherent event.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_potentialOutcome_eq_gFormula
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.65: the longitudinal g-formula for discrete covariates. Covariates `L t` take values in a finite type and treatments `A t` in any type, at times `t = 0, …, T`; `l` ranges over covariate records `(l_0, …, l_T)`, `Ya` is the potential outcome under the regime `a` and `Y` the observed outcome. Consistency is `Y = Ya` whenever the observed treatments follow the regime. Sequential exchangeability is used in its mean form, `E[Ya 1{A_t = a_t} | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}] = E[Ya | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}] P(A_t = a_t | …)`, written without division; it is implied by `Ya ⊥ A_t | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}`. Sequential positivity is the uniform lower bound `δ` on `P(A_t = a_t | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1})`. The `t = 0` factor of the product is `P(L_0 = l_0)`, since the regime-adherent past before time `0` is the whole space. The iterated-conditional-expectation form and the general kernel form are not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialDispersionLaw

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalGLMLogLikelihood

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCanonicalGLMRoot

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_canonicalGLM_root
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.3, canonical-link form: for independent and identically distributed pairs `(xᵢ, Yᵢ)` whose response given the covariate is exponential-dispersion with natural parameter `⟪x, β⟫`, with covariates bounded by `R`, smooth cumulant function, natural parameter space all of `ℝ`, and nonsingular `J = E[x xᵀ b''(⟪x, β⟫)]`, every consistent root `β̂` of the likelihood equations satisfies `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, φ J⁻¹)`, and `φ̂^{-1/2} J^{1/2} √n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, I_p)` for every consistent `φ̂`. Restrictions of scope: canonical link (`g = (b')⁻¹`), bounded covariates, and natural parameter space `ℝ`; the general twice-differentiable link is not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_canonicalGLM_deviance

Hypotheses as in `tendstoInDistribution_canonicalGLM_root`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_linearSEMLaw_eq_of_equalVariance

The noise means are arbitrary.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_additiveNoiseLaw_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, nonlinear additive Gaussian-noise models: if two additive-noise models along `G` and `H`, with three times continuously differentiable structural functions that respect the parents and are nonlinear in each parent argument, and independent Gaussian noises of positive variances, have the same law, then `G = H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_linearGaussianSEM_iff_markovEquivalent

Faithfulness is the hypothesis under which the equivalence class is the precise answer.

declarations.name: CKSD.andRuleEdge

declarations.name: CKSD.orRuleEdge

declarations.name: CKSD.neighbourhoodSelection_graph_recovery
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.53, neighbourhood selection: with universal constants, under incoherence, the row-sum bound, unit-bounded variances, maximal degree `m`, and `n ≥ c₁ m log p`, the "or" rule includes no false edge and the "and" rule includes every edge with `|Θ j k| ≥ 7 b λ max (Θ j j) (Θ k k)`, with the stated probability; since the "and" edges are "or" edges, both rules have both properties. The edge condition bounds the regression coefficients `-Θ j k / Θ j j` and `-Θ k j / Θ k k` below by `7 b λ`; this is the bound proved by Wainwright (2019), Theorem 11.12, whose statement puts `|Θ j k|` in its place although `Θ j j ≥ 1` is not bounded above. The lasso estimates `B x j` are arbitrary minimizers.

declarations.name: CKSD.grenanderEstimator

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNonincreasingDensity

declarations.name: CKSD.twoSidedBrownianPath

declarations.name: CKSD.IsChernoffArgmax

declarations.name: CKSD.grenanderEstimator_isMaximumLikelihood
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.11: the Grenander estimator is a nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator among nonincreasing densities on `[0, ∞)`. Scope: a fixed sample of `n ≥ 1` positive observations; the estimator is extended by zero to the nonpositive half-line, and the likelihood is the product of density values at the observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_grenanderEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.11: the cube-root limit law of the Grenander estimator at an interior point. The density `f` is a version vanishing on the negative half-line, positive and nonincreasing on `[0, ∞)`, and differentiable at `x₀ > 0` with negative derivative (which gives continuity at `x₀`); the limit is the law of `|4 f(x₀) f'(x₀)| ^ (1/3) Z` for Chernoff's `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_isLogConcaveProjection

declarations.name: CKSD.coxPartialLikelihood_asymptotics

declarations.name: CKSD.jumpIntegral

declarations.name: CKSD.countingMartingaleTransform

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_countingMartingaleTransform
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.34: Rebolledo's central limit theorem for counting-process martingale transforms, in finite-dimensional form: under convergence in probability of the predictable variations to a continuous deterministic `V` with positive-semidefinite increments and the Lindeberg condition, the values of `M^{(n)}` at finitely many times in `[0, τ]` converge jointly in law to those of the continuous Gaussian martingale with covariance `V(s ∧ t)`. Restrictions: the compensated counting processes are martingales rather than local martingales, all processes live on one probability space, and weak convergence in `D[0,τ]^k` is replaced by convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockMean

declarations.name: CKSD.movingBlockBootstrapLaw

declarations.name: CKSD.movingBlockBootstrap_consistent
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.11: consistency of the moving-block bootstrap for the mean of a strictly stationary strongly mixing sequence with `𝔼|X|^{2+δ} < ∞` and `∑ α(k)^{δ/(2+δ)} < ∞`: the autocovariances are absolutely summable, `√n (X̄_n - μ) ⇒ N(0, σ²_∞)`, and the Kolmogorov distance between the bootstrap law and the law of `√n (X̄_n - μ)` tends to `0` in probability, for block lengths `b → ∞` with `b/n → 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.stein_linearPrediction_equivalent_gaussian
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.21: Stein's theorem on asymptotically efficient prediction under equivalent Gaussian laws. The coordinates are linearly independent under `k₀`, the laws `P₀` and `P₁` are centred Gaussian with covariances `k₀` and `k₁`, and `ψ` ranges over the closed linear span `H` of the coordinates in `L²(P₀)`. Uniformly over `ψ ∈ H` with nonzero `P₀`-error, the relative excess error of the `k₁`-predictor and the relative misstatement of its error tend to zero; the exchanged roles are the same statement applied to `(k₁, P₁, k₀, P₀)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_periodogram_div_spectralDensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.6: periodogram ordinates at Fourier frequencies nearest to fixed frequencies in `(0, π)`, divided by the spectral density, converge jointly in law to independent standard exponential variables, for a linear process with absolutely summable coefficients and iid innovations of finite positive variance. The non-consistency corollary is not restated.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_lagWindowEstimator_moments
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.6: asymptotic mean and variance, and mean-square consistency, of a lag-window spectral estimator for a linear process with `∑ |ψ_j| |j|^{1/2} < ∞` and iid innovations with finite fourth moment, when the truncation point `r` satisfies `r → ∞` and `r/n → 0`. The window is assumed continuous at `0` (see `IsLagWindow`).

declarations.name: CKSD.infDist_past_sq_eq_kolmogorov
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.16: Kolmogorov's (Szegő's) formula for the one-step prediction error of a centred weakly stationary sequence from its infinite past. Here `X` lies in a complex inner-product space, `⟪X s, X t⟫ = γ(t - s)`, the spectral measure `F` lives on `(-π, π]`, and `f` is the density of its absolutely continuous part. The value `0` is taken exactly when `log f` fails to be integrable or `f` vanishes on a set of positive measure, i.e. when `∫ log f = -∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.arPolynomial
declarations.doc: The autoregressive polynomial `φ(z) = 1 - ∑_{i=1}^p φ_i z^i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.maPolynomial
declarations.doc: The moving-average polynomial `θ(z) = 1 + ∑_{j=1}^q θ_j z^j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaSpectralShape
declarations.doc: The ARMA spectral shape `g(x; β) = |θ(e^{-ix})|² / |φ(e^{-ix})|²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lastArCoefficient
declarations.doc: The last autoregressive coefficient `φ_p`, read as `0` when `p = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lastMaCoefficient
declarations.doc: The last moving-average coefficient `θ_q`, read as `0` when `q = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaAdmissibleParameters
declarations.doc: Causal, invertible, identifiable ARMA(p,q) parameters: `φ(z) θ(z) ≠ 0` on the closed unit disc, no common zeros, and `(φ_p, θ_q) ≠ (0,0)` (vacuous for `p = q = 0`).

declarations.name: CKSD.whittleObjective
declarations.doc: The Whittle objective `n⁻¹ ∑_j I_n(ω_j) / g(ω_j; β)` over the Fourier frequencies `ω_j = 2πj/n`, `0 ≤ j < n`; by `2π`-periodicity this equals the sum over `(-π, π]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaAsymptoticInformation
declarations.doc: The asymptotic information matrix `W(β) = (4π)⁻¹ ∫_{-π}^{π} ∇ log g ∇ log gᵀ` of ARMA estimation.

declarations.name: CKSD.whittleEstimator_asymptotics
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.17, Whittle-estimator case: for a causal invertible ARMA(p,q) process with iid, not necessarily Gaussian, innovations of variance `σ² > 0`, every measurable approximate minimizer of the Whittle objective over the admissible parameters (to within `(n+1)⁻²`) is strongly consistent, the Whittle innovation-variance estimator `2π · min` converges almost surely to `σ²`, and `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, W(β)⁻¹)`. The process is any `L²`-bounded solution of the ARMA equations, which is the stationary causal solution. The Gaussian maximum-likelihood and least-squares estimators, and the autoregressive identity `W⁻¹ = σ² Γ_p⁻¹`, are not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralRandomField
declarations.doc: Spectral random-phase field for a spectral measure of total real mass `mass`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_stationary_field_of_spectral_measure
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.24: a finite spectral measure is realized by a mean-square continuous stationary field. This concerns the Fourier/random-field assertion, not Matérn differentiability.

declarations.name: CKSD.logLikelihoodPartialSum
declarations.doc: Partial sums of iid log-likelihood increments.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_stopped_exponential_eq_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.41: Wald's fundamental stopped exponential identity at a first exit time. The finite-valued time `N` is a version of the almost surely finite first exit.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_nelsonAalenEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.28, fixed-time Nelson–Aalen CLT for absolutely continuous failure times.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_kaplanMeierEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.29, fixed-time Kaplan–Meier CLT under independent censoring.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_martingale_array_sum
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.1: triangular-array martingale central limit theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_wold_decomposition
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.2, Wold decomposition of a stationary sequence in a real Hilbert space.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sample_autocorrelations
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.4, independent-observation special case of Bartlett's theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: The lag-counting weight `#{(i, j) : i, j < n, i - j = h} / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sum_eq_tsum_lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: A normalized double sum over `i, j < n` of a function of `i - j`, regrouped by lag.

declarations.name: CKSD.lagCountWeight_nonneg
declarations.doc: Lag-counting weights are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.lagCountWeight_le_one
declarations.doc: Lag-counting weights are at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: The lower bound `(n - |h|)/n` for the lag-counting weight.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: Lag-counting weights tend to one at each fixed lag.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_normalized_variance_eq_tsum_covariance
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.12, long-run variance from summable autocovariances.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_stationary_gaussian_process_of_posSemidef
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.14, real Gaussian realization of a positive-definite stationary covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.garch_series_summable_and_moments
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.18, finite-variance GARCH series when `alpha + beta < 1`.
